short: The total ingredient cost of one served portion.
seoTitle: Plate Cost — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Plate cost is the total cost of everything that reaches the customer in one serving — main ingredients, sauces, garnish, oil and packaging.
definition: Plate cost is the total cost of everything that reaches the customer in one serving — main ingredients, sauces, garnish, oil and packaging. It is the output of recipe costing and the input to menu pricing.
bodyHtml:
Why Plate Cost matters

Plate cost is what makes a menu price defensible. Two dishes at the same price can differ by a hundred rupees in plate cost, and only one of them is worth promoting.

Plate Cost formula

Plate cost = Ingredient cost + Garnish + Consumables + Packaging

Menu price should be set from plate cost and a target food cost percentage.

How Plate Cost works in practice

Include the small things: the extra chutney, the paper liner, the delivery container. Individually trivial, they routinely add five to ten percent to the real cost of a portion.

faq.question: Should packaging be in plate cost?
faq.answer: For delivery orders, absolutely. It is a real per-order cost that only appears when you count it.

faq.question: How do I use plate cost to set a menu price?
faq.answer: Divide plate cost by your target food cost percentage — a ₹90 plate at a 30% target implies a ₹300 menu price.

formula.expression: Plate cost = Ingredient cost + Garnish + Consumables + Packaging
